name: Percentage Change
description: Calculate the percentage change between two values.
formula: Percentage change = (New value − Old value) / Old value × 100
business_contexts: a company tracking revenue from one quarter to the next
a retailer comparing foot traffic year over year
a factory comparing output between two shifts
an airline comparing ticket prices between two seasons
a subscription service comparing signups month to month
question_patterns: Given the starting and ending values below, what is the percentage change?
Calculate the percentage change between the two values shown.
By what percentage did the value change, given the figures below?
What is the percent change from the first figure to the second, shown below?
Using the values given, calculate the percentage change.
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate percentage change = (value_after − value_before) / value_before × 100
key_insight: Percentage change is always measured against the starting value, never the ending value — the base of the fraction never moves.
common_mistakes: Dividing by the ending value instead of the starting value
Forgetting to multiply by 100 and reporting a decimal fraction as if it were a percentage
framework_soundbite: Change over start, always — the denominator is where you began, not where you ended up.
